macro: US equity indices are mixed at midday with the S&P 500 flat, Nasdaq up 38 basis points, and the Dow down 43 basis points. Markets are in a holding pattern as investors await developments at the UN regarding Iran and the Middle East. Brent crude is off modestly around $100 on hopes for a diplomatic resolution and the partial resumption of Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline.
rates_fed: Treasuries are pretty flat across the curve with no major rate moves to speak of midday. No Fed commentary is highlighted in today's update. The dollar and rates are not a primary driver of today's session.
market_outlook: Adam's tone is cautiously neutral — the market is waiting on two major near-term catalysts: a potential Middle East/Iran diplomatic breakthrough at the UN, and a critical 10-day stretch of AI events including Meta's Connect keynote Wednesday night, OpenAI's DevDay on September 29th, and Micron earnings on September 30th. The setup is mixed rather than clearly directional, with sector rotation visible beneath the flat index surface.
bull_case: AI names are outperforming broadly ahead of a loaded catalyst calendar that could re-accelerate the theme. Housing stocks are showing strength alongside consumer staples and travel/leisure, suggesting broadening participation. AutoZone's management commentary on positive comp linearity through the quarter provides a constructive read on consumer spending. The Iran situation at the UN offers potential for a positive geopolitical surprise that could lift energy uncertainty.
bear_case: Financials are broadly weak with banks, brokers, insurers, and asset managers all underperforming — a concerning signal given their market weight and economic sensitivity. CMS rate cuts are hitting lab testing names harder than expected, and managed care is also under pressure, pointing to healthcare reimbursement headwinds. THO Industries flagged a difficult macro landscape in its earnings miss, and the SB Energy IPO delay suggests cooling sentiment on the data center boom at the margin. Trump's approval sinking to a career-low 32% raises political risk heading into the mid-terms.

company_items.summary: AutoZone beat fiscal Q4 EPS at $56.05 versus the Street's $54.03, but quality was low — the beat was driven by tariff refunds adding 145 basis points to gross margins and a non-cash LIFO impact adding 105 basis points. Domestic comps came in at +1.6% versus the Street's +3.1%, though management noted positive sales linearity through the quarter, which is providing some reassurance to investors.

MillerKnoll reported strong fiscal Q1 EPS of 53 cents versus the Street's 36 cents, and importantly the beat holds up even excluding tariff refunds — adjusting for the 11-cent tailwind, EPS was still 42 cents versus 36 cents expected. Guidance was mixed with fiscal 2027 sales range trimmed but EPS outlook left unchanged.

THOR Industries missed fiscal Q4 EPS at 78 cents versus the Street's 87 cents, with gross margin weakness of 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4% versus the Street's 13.85% more than offsetting slightly better-than-expected revenue of $2.311 billion. Management explicitly flagged a difficult macro landscape, which is a cautious signal for the RV industry.

Meta's Muse personal AI agent is seeing surging downloads ahead of Zuckerberg's keynote at Meta Connect Wednesday night at 7pm ET, with investor expectations building. Shopify confirmed it will allow Muse to complete purchases on its platform — in contrast to Amazon, which blocked Muse — giving Meta a meaningful e-commerce distribution win.

Shopify will allow Meta's Muse AI agent to complete purchases on its e-commerce platform, a notable partnership win that differentiates Shopify from Amazon, which blocked Muse. This positions Shopify as a preferred destination for agentic AI commerce.

Quest Diagnostics shares were hit following new Medicare payment rates from CMS for lab services that represented a larger reduction than the market had anticipated. The negative rate surprise is pressuring the entire lab testing group.

Lab Corp shares fell alongside Quest Diagnostics after CMS released new Medicare lab service payment rates with cuts deeper than expected. Both names are under meaningful selling pressure on the reimbursement news.

Cognex announced the acquisition of RealSense, described as the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and physical AI, for approximately $500 million upfront plus an additional $106.5 million. This is a direct bet on the physical AI and robotics buildout.

Viking Therapeutics reported positive trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, including 22% weight loss, a strong efficacy readout that keeps the company competitive in the increasingly crowded obesity drug space.

On Holdings held its analyst day and outlined a plan to reach 2029 sales of at least CHF 5.6 billion versus the Street's CHF 5.4 billion, with EBITDA margins above 22% versus the Street's 21% estimate. The company also authorized a $1 billion share buyback, adding a capital return element to the growth story.

sectors: Financials broadly weak — banks, brokers, insurers, and asset managers all underperforming, a notable sector-wide drag. AI and semiconductor names outperforming with ARM, ASML, GOOGL, META, MU, ORCL, and others in the green ahead of a critical catalyst calendar. Housing stocks DHI, LEN, and PHM showing strength. Auto parts retailers rallying on AZO's positive linearity commentary, lifting GPC and ORLY. Lab testing names DGX and LH hit hard on CMS rate cuts. Managed care CNC, ELV, and HUM also under pressure. Aerospace and defense names broadly weak. Texas Governor Abbott's order halting new data center permits adds a regulatory overhang for the data center buildout in that state.

tts_summary: Here's your midday update for Tuesday September 22nd. Markets are in a holding pattern. The S&P 500 is essentially flat, the Nasdaq is up about 38 basis points, the Russell 2000 is up 30 basis points, but the Dow is down 43 basis points. Under the hood, it's a clear rotation story — tech and AI are working, financials are not. Treasuries are flat across the curve. Brent is hovering near one hundred dollars a barrel, off modestly on hopes that United Nations talks could produce some kind of Iran breakthrough. Saudi Arabia is also signaling that its East-West Pipeline may be coming back online, which is taking some of the geopolitical premium out of crude. The big macro theme right now is that investors are essentially in a wait-and-see mode ahead of what could be a market-moving ten days for AI — we get Zuckerberg's keynote at Meta Connect tomorrow night, OpenAI's DevDay on the 29th, and then Micron earnings on September 30th. That calendar is keeping buyers interested in the AI complex despite the flat index action. On the earnings front, AutoZone beat on fiscal fourth quarter earnings per share, coming in at fifty-six dollars and five cents versus the Street at fifty-four dollars and three cents. But the quality was not great — tariff refunds added 145 basis points to gross margins and a non-cash inventory impact added another 105 basis points. Domestic comps missed, coming in at plus one point six percent versus the Street's three point one percent. The saving grace was management saying comp linearity was positive through the quarter, which is lifting auto parts peers like Genuine Parts and O'Reilly. MillerKnoll was a cleaner beat — 53 cents versus 36 cents expected, and they still would have beaten even stripping out tariff refund help. Thor Industries missed and management flagged a tough macro environment, which is worth watching as a read on the consumer. On the AI side, Meta's Muse personal AI agent is seeing surging downloads ahead of tomorrow's keynote, and Shopify confirmed it will allow Muse to complete purchases on its platform — a win over Amazon, which blocked Muse. Viking Therapeutics reported 22 percent weight loss in its GLP-1 trial, keeping it in the conversation in obesity. On the negative side, Quest Diagnostics and Lab Corp are getting hit hard after CMS released Medicare lab payment rates with cuts deeper than expected. That's pressuring the whole lab testing group. Cognex announced a roughly five hundred million dollar acquisition of depth-sensing camera maker RealSense, a direct play on physical AI and robotics. The bear case today centers on the financial sector weakness — banks, brokers, insurers, and asset managers are all broadly lower, which is a meaningful signal to monitor. The bull case is the AI catalyst calendar and the breadth of outperformance in tech and semis. Stay focused on Meta tomorrow night — that keynote could set the tone for the rest of the week.
